correctness.rationale: The source fixes Ag={a1,a2,a3,b,c} and AP={pb,pc,pS,pA,pM}. Inspection of the reduction shows that Good uses temporal depth at most two, Mem uses XXpb, Eq adds only strategy quantification, and Succ/Add/Mult use one X. The dagger translation adds only strategy quantifiers and Boolean connectives, prenex conversion preserves temporal occurrences, and the injectivizing padding is propositional. Therefore the source's one-one lower reduction lands in the claimed fragment. Proposition 3.1 gives an injective upper translation for all SL formulas and hence for the fragment; Myhill yields computable isomorphism.

originality.rationale: The published theorem states hardness for the next-time Boolean-goal fragment but does not state fixed vocabulary or temporal depth two. The full proof was checked for those stronger properties, and candidate-specific published-finding and literature searches found no equivalent statement.
residual_risks: Because the fixed vocabulary and X/XX patterns are explicit in the source proof, specialists may regard the refinement as an immediate but unstated corollary.
No minimality is claimed: fewer agents, fewer propositions, or temporal depth one may already suffice.
The reduction still uses an unbounded action domain, so the result does not challenge known bounded-action decidability phenomena.

value.rationale: Temporal depth and vocabulary size are natural syntactic resources in modal and temporal logics. The result shows that neither deep temporal reasoning nor an expanding agent/proposition vocabulary causes Strategy Logic's second-order complexity: the full hardness is already present at depth two over ten fixed modal symbols, leaving strategy quantification as the unbounded resource. This sharpens the source's next-time-fragment result and identifies depth one as a concrete remaining boundary.
